fix_commit_message:
Bug 1987290 - Part 1: Use get() instead of operator[] to get arguments in FinalizationRegistryObject::unregister. r=jonco

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D264002
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 2b8155c2c4c2 on top of intro 321172222a2e via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): FinalizationRegistryObject::unregister() in SpiderMonkey reads its first argument using the unchecked CallArgs::operator[] (`args[0]`) before validating that an argument was actually supplied, instead of using the bounds-safe `args.get(0)`. Calling `FinalizationRegistry.prototype.unregister` with zero arguments (e.g. `new FinalizationRegistry(()=>{}).unregister()`) causes an out-of-bounds read of the native call's argument vector, tripping a debug assertion (`i < argc_` in js/public/CallArgs.h) and causing undefined behavior / a security-relevant OOB read in release/optimized builds. Root cause: Bug 1863140 Part 3 (commit 321172222a2e) refactored FinalizationRegistry.register/unregister to support non-object (e.g. symbol) targets/unregister tokens via a new CanBeHeldWeakly() helper. While doing so, the unregister() function's existing safe pattern of `args.get(0).isObject()` followed by `&args[0].toObject()` (indexing only after confirming the argument existed and was an object) was replaced by directly constructing `RootedValue unregisterToken(cx, args[0])` ahead of any validation, re-introducing an unchecked array index into the native call arguments before verifying argc covers that index.
